name: story_A_jar
description: Story frame draft A: credits that a phone app adds every day, and a jar of strangers whose contents grow and are always divided equally.

rules.text: - A phone app you use has opened a jar for {n} of its users: you and {n_others} other people whom you do not know. Nobody in the jar can contact anybody else in it.
- The jar runs for several days; this question is about a single day.
- The jar runs for {rounds} days, with the same {n} users every day.
- At the start of every day the app adds {endowment} credits to the balance of each user, free of charge. Credits can be spent in the app like cash.
- Each user then decides how many of these new credits (a whole number from 0 to {endowment}) to put into the jar. Credits that are not put into the jar stay in the user's balance.

- At the end of the day the app makes the jar {multiplier} times as large. The jar has a fixed rule: everything in it is divided equally among the {n} users, no matter who put in how much. So every credit put into the jar brings {mpcr} credits to each of the {n} users. Your part of the jar in a day is therefore:
{mpcr} x (credits put into the jar by all {n} users together)
- What you end a day with is the credits you kept plus your part of the jar:
{endowment} - (credits you put into the jar) + {mpcr} x (credits put into the jar by all {n} users together)

- After the amounts of a day are shown, each user may also make reductions (0 to {max_punish}) to the balance of each other user. Each reduction costs the user who makes it {punish_cost} credit(s) and removes {punish_impact} credits from the other user's balance. A user learns only the total number of reductions made to their balance, not who made them.
- After each day you see how many credits each user put into the jar and what you ended the day with.

history.empty:
EARLIER DAYS
This is the first day; there are no earlier days yet.
history.contributions: Put into the jar: {contributions_list}. Jar total before it grew: {group_total}.
round: Your part of the jar: {project_share}. What you ended the day with: {round_earnings}.
round_P: Reductions made to your balance: {received} (credits removed: {points_lost}).
What you ended the day with after reductions: {final_earnings}.

contribute:
DAY {round_no} of {rounds}. You are {me}. All users choose at the same time, without seeing each other's choice for this day.
How many of your {endowment} new credits do you put into the jar? (a whole number from 0 to {endowment})
punish:
DAY {round_no} of {rounds}, reduction step. You are {me}.
This day: {contributions} Your part of the jar this day: {project_share}. What you end this day with (before reductions): {earnings}.
You may now make reductions (0 to {max_punish}) to the balance of each other user. Each reduction costs you {punish_cost} credit(s) and removes {punish_impact} credits from that user's balance. Your total cost may not exceed what you end this day with, so you can make at most {max_points} reductions in total. All users choose at the same time.

fixed_round.question:
QUESTION
This is day {round_no} of {rounds}. On the previous day the other {n_others} users of your jar put in, on average, {others_mean} credits each.
How many of your {endowment} new credits do you put into the jar on this day? (a whole number from 0 to {endowment})

questions.text: Suppose that on a day you put {own} credits into the jar and the other {n_others} users put in {other_1}, {other_2} and {other_3} credits. How many credits do you end that day with?

Suppose that the other users put the same amounts into the jar. If you put {delta} more credits into the jar, by how much does what you end that day with change? Give the change as a whole number (it can be positive, zero or negative).

response.rationale_description: One or two sentences on why you chose this.
response.punishment_description: Reductions per other user, keyed by user number.
